Archival Dispatch: 30 Master Broadcasts Dated Across Early Acoustic Recordings, American History (Casey Stengel & Pershing), Aunt Mary, and Easy Aces

Date: 2026-08-21
Author: radio index

Tags: Early Recordings, Billy Murray, Cal Stewart, American History, Casey Stengel, General Pershing, Richard Nixon, Theodore Roosevelt, Aunt Mary, Easy Aces, Goodman Ace, Original Filenames
Raw Markdown

Batch 47 Forensic Discoveries

Batch 47 resolves 30 historic recordings across foundational acoustic sound recording, pivotal 20th-century historical moments, and classic comedy: 8 turn-of-the-century cylinder and 78 RPM master recordings from Early Recordings (1904–1917, featuring Billy Murray's The Yankee Doodle Boy, Cal Stewart's Uncle Josh, and Frank Stanley), 8 landmark documentary and spoken-word broadcasts from American History Through The Eyes Of Radio (featuring General Pershing's 1918 address from France, Casey Stengel's hilarious 1958 Congressional baseball testimony, and Richard Nixon's 1968 campaign address), 6 sequential chapters from Aunt Mary (1946), and 8 sequential 1938 comedy episodes from Goodman and Jane Ace's Easy Aces.

1. Early Acoustic Recordings — 1904–1917 Acoustic Master Cylinders & 78s

Early sound pioneers recorded in New York and Camden, New Jersey:

Original Circulating Filename Canonical Title Verified Airdate / Release Legendary Performance
Early_Murray_Yankee_Doodle.mp3 "Billy Murray: 'The Yankee Doodle Boy' (Victor 4575)" 1905-01-20 George M. Cohan's Little Johnny Jones anthem sung by Billy Murray.
Early_Murray_Cheyenne.mp3 "Billy Murray: 'Cheyenne' (Victor 4719)" 1906-04-18 Pioneer western cowboy pop song recorded for Victor.
Early_Uncle_Josh_Automobile.mp3 "Cal Stewart: 'Uncle Josh on an Automobile' (Columbia Cylinder)" 1904-09-15 Rural storytelling and humor from Pumpkin Center.
Early_Frank_Stanley_I_Want.mp3 "Frank Stanley: 'I Want What I Want When I Want It' (Victor 4945)" 1906-11-12 Victor Herbert's operatic showstopper from Mlle. Modiste.
Early_Quartet_Everybody_Two_Step.mp3 "American Quartet: 'Everybody Two-Step' (Victor 17124)" 1912-07-23 Ragtime four-part harmony vocal performance.
Early_Morgan_Stanley_Reuben.mp3 "Corinne Morgan & Frank Stanley: 'Reuben and Cynthia'" 1904-05-10 Vaudeville conversational duet recording.
Early_MacColl_Campbells_Coming.mp3 "John MacColl: 'The Campbells Are Coming' (Bagpipe Solo)" 1908-08-14 Rare early acoustic bagpipe recording.
Early_Good_Bye_Broadway.mp3 "American Quartet: 'Good-Bye Broadway, Hello France' (Victor 18330)" 1917-06-28 WWI doughboy marching anthem recorded as US entered the war.
